Method of Attack: Utilizes SSH credentials found on compromised systems to propagate itself across networks
Searches common directories and files where SSH keys and credentials are typically stored, such as .ssh directories and config files
Parses shell history files (e.g., .bash_history, .zsh_history) to identify commands referencing SSH private keys
Utilizes the 'find_from_bash_history' feature to parse bash history for SSH-related commands
Analyzes system logs and network cache (ARP tables) to pinpoint potential targets and gather information leading to private key discovery
Impacted Systems: Enterprise environments using SSH for secure connections
Attack Vector: Lateral movement within a network using discovered SSH keys
Fileless nature makes it challenging to detect
Indicators of Compromise: SSH keys found in .ssh directories and config files
Commands referencing SSH private keys in shell history files (e.g., .bash_history, .zsh_history)
System logs and network cache (ARP tables) showing unusual activity related to SSH connections
